ctx.title: Sameera Reddy remembers Nana Patekar, says actor ‘quietly supported many charities and donated heavily’ | Interview
ctx.summary: Sameera Reddy says Nana Patekar’s generous, low-profile support for charities earned her deep respect while they worked together on Taxi No. 9211.
ctx.text:
Actor Sameera Reddy worked with Nana Patekar in two films, the 2006 comedy thriller Taxi No. 9211 and the 2003 horror anthology Darna Mana Hai. In a recent conversation with Hindustan Times, Sameera shared memories of the late actor, who died on October 8. Recalling her experience of working with him early in her career, the actor said that while she had a lot to learn from Nana as a performer, it was his philanthropic work that earned her immense respect.
Sameera shared that while Nana is remembered for his exceptional acting, he was also a philanthropist who quietly donated generously to support several charities. She said, “During Taxi No. 9211, I was still a newcomer in the industry. Beyond his acting, what many people never realised was what an extraordinary philanthropist Nana Patekar was. He quietly supported a lot of charities and he donated heavily, but he was never the kind of actor to speak about it or seek publicity. I only found out while shooting on that film about the many institutions whom he supported silently. I had tremendous respect at that moment for him, because while many actors constantly talk about their good deeds, he did everything quietly without anyone knowing about it. That's when I had a new-found respect for him on top of him being the incredible actor he was.”
Sameera added that she also learnt a great deal about acting from Nana, particularly while watching him perform in the film. She said, “Also, John and me were still young and newbies and there was so much to learn from his style of acting. The way he played that completely crazy taxi driver, who had so many layers and there was a lot to learn from him as an actor. But I still have so much respect for what he was doing beyond being an actor.”
Directed by Milan Luthria, Taxi No 9211 starred Nana Patekar as Raghav Shastri, a taxi driver, and John Abraham as Jai Mittal, a wealthy businessman whose paths cross and their lives became entangled over the course of a day. Sameera played Rupali, Jai's girlfriend, while Sonali Kulkarni also featured in the film.
Nana Patekar died at the age of 75 on October 8, 2026. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors attempted to revive him with CPR for around 45 minutes but could not save him. He died in Goa. His postmortem report later confirmed that he died of a heart attack.
Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows.

A self-confessed cinephile who breathes Hindi cinema, Vibha can often be found sacrificing sleep after binge-watching films and web series. Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today.

At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through film reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, celebrity interviews, and trend-driven stories. She later brought her storytelling and editorial expertise to The Indian Express, where she continued to deepen her understanding of cinema through long-form entertainment explainers, retrospectives and feature writing.
